Subject: Immediate: transient conversational hold affecting streaming responses

Hi Ava / FluxPay SRE team,

I wanted to let you know we are actively investigating an issue that started at ~07:50 PT this morning that caused a small subset of streaming chat requests to enter a "conversational hold" state (partial output, delayed continuation). You may have observed truncated responses or longer-than-usual time until the final token for affected sessions.

What we know so far:
- Impact: ~0.6% of streaming generation requests for FluxPay (hosted) experienced one or more 8–30s stalls before completion. No tokens were lost; some responses required retry or resumed after a backfill.
- Root cause (initial triage): an unexpected token-accounting mismatch in the streaming pipeline that triggered aggressive per-request backpressure and a short-lived queueing surge on the prefetch/batching layer.
- Mitigation in flight: we applied a targeted throttling override and widened the token accounting window which immediately reduced the tail stalls.

Immediate ask from us:
- Can you share any customer-facing intercepts we've missed (webhooks, client retry behaviors) so we can correlate?
- If you have active sessions that you believe were affected, please reply to this thread with request IDs (if available).

Next steps from Redwood:
- Full incident trace and logs are attached (excerpt) and we will post a short incident note on our status page within the hour.
- Engineering will remain in the bridge for the next 3–4 hours to verify stability and follow-up with a post-incident summary.

Attachments: incident_log_excerpt.txt (trace of affected requests), screenshot-streaming-trace.png

I'm very sorry for the disruption. Marissa and Ben are already coordinating the rollback plan if we observe any regression during validation.

Best,
Monica

Subject: RE: Immediate: transient conversational hold affecting streaming responses — technical update

Thanks team. Quick technical summary from runtime:

Timeline & cause (short):
- 07:49 PT: sudden delta between token-update acknowledgments from the streaming proxy and the batcher state machine. The mismatch caused the batcher to mark some inflight sessions as "awaiting tokens" and apply per-request backpressure.
- 07:50–08:00 PT: the backpressure created a micro-queue at the prefetch layer; continuous batching attempted to compensate which introduced 2–3x more latency on affected buckets.

Mitigation performed by us (08:06 PT):
- Increased token-accounting window + disabled the aggressive final-token backpressure rule for 15 minutes while we flushed the micro-queue.
- Rebalanced prefetched shards to avoid hot spots for customer-specific routing keys.

Customer impact details:
- Approx 0.6% of FluxPay's streaming requests observed 8–30s additional delay; non-streaming text/generation calls were unaffected.
- No data exposure or token loss.

Operational notes & guidance for customers:
- Recommended client behavior: do not retry immediately on a streaming stall. Prefer a short linear backoff (2–5s) then reconnect to obtain the remaining tokens — this minimizes retry amplification.
- If you see client-side timeouts, surface the request IDs and we will map them to server traces (we can accept up to 48 hours of IDs).

Next actions:
- We will keep the relaxed backpressure rule in place for one hour and run a gradual re-enable with a canary to validate correctness.
- Postmortem doc + timeline will be published in 48 hours.

Ben Carter
VP, Platform Reliability — Redwood Inference

Subject: Follow-up: incident cleared and next steps (postmortem timeline)

Hi Ava — quick follow-up now that we've validated the mitigation across your tenant and broader host pool.

Summary:
- Status: mitigated and resolved at 12:02 PT. We observed no further conversational holds in the last three hours for FluxPay traffic.
- Scope: affected only streaming chat endpoints; estimated 0.6% of sessions experienced elongated tails (8–30s).
- Root cause (preliminary): an edge-case token-accounting race between the streaming proxy and continuous batcher which only surfaced under a particular sequence of partial-token acknowledgements.

What we did:
- Emergency mitigation: widened the accounting window and temporarily disabled the final-token backpressure rule to allow in-flight sessions to drain.
- Engineering follow-ups: a code change is being staged to remove the race and add stricter unit coverage for token ACK handling. A gradual canary re-enable will happen after the fix (ETA: 48–72 hours).

What we recommend for customers right now:
- Client retry guidance: implement a 2–5s linear backoff before reconnecting to a streaming session to avoid retry storms. We updated our public client guidance here: https://docs.redwood.ai/streaming-retries
- If you have request IDs for affected sessions, please send them to us. We'll map them into our traces (up to 48 hours).

Attachments: incident_log_excerpt.txt, screenshot-streaming-trace.png

We will publish a postmortem within 48 hours that includes a timeline, root cause analysis, and corrective actions. Marissa will reach out if we need to coordinate customer-specific notifications beyond this thread.

Appreciate your patience and apologies for the disruption.

Best,
